prompt:

Context: workload=coding-agent; framework=LangGraph; model to evaluate=moonshotai/Kimi-K2.7-Code.

# Coding Agent Framework & Model Recommendation

Generated by Nebius Integration Scout · 2026-11-02 · endpoint https://api.tokenfactory.nebius.com/v1/

**Verdict:** integration verified · recommended model `moonshotai/Kimi-K2.7-Code` · workload coding-agent · no latency budget given

## What was proven
- langgraph on daytona: tool call verified — LangGraph ReAct agent successfully called weather tool with city=Amsterdam
- pydantic_ai on daytona: tool call verified — PydanticAI with typed tool and typed output successfully completed

Conformance kit: 12 pass · 1 partial · 0 fail (cache.cached_tokens=PARTIAL: prefix cache not observable)

| model | TTFT ms | tokens/s | prefix-cache hit (tokens) |
|---|---|---|---|
| moonshotai/Kimi-K2.7-Code | 1463.8 | 1658.7 | 0 |
| MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash | 3215.2 | 100.3 | 256 |

## Findings
- moonshotai/Kimi-K2.7-Code delivers 1,659 tokens/s, 16.5x faster than MiniMax-M3.1-Flash (100 tokens/s)
- LangGraph and PydanticAI both verified with tool_called=true on Daytona
- Conformance passed 12/13 checks; prefix cache not observable
- Kimi-K2.7-Code TTFT is 1.5s, MiniMax-M3.1-Flash TTFT is 3.2s
- Kimi-K2.7-Code handled parallel tool calls and JSON schema output correctly
- PydanticAI probe used typed tools and structured output with full roundtrip

## Next steps
- Start with PydanticAI for type safety and performance
- Monitor Daytona sandbox stability for long-running agents
- File a ticket to enable prefix caching for Kimi-K2.7-Code
- Run longitudinal benchmarks on full coding tasks

## Cost
add prices to pricing.json for an estimate

## Integration
```python
from langchain_core.tools import tool
from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI
from langgraph.prebuilt import create_react_agent

llm = ChatOpenAI(model="moonshotai/Kimi-K2.7-Code", base_url="https://api.tokenfactory.nebius.com/v1/", api_key=NEBIUS_API_KEY, temperature=0)

@tool
def your_tool(arg: str) -> dict:
    """What the tool does."""
    ...

agent = create_react_agent(llm, [your_tool])
state = agent.invoke({"messages": [("user", "...")]})
```

attributes.gen_ai.system_instructions:
[{"type":"text","content":"You are a Nebius forward-deployed engineer. A partner has asked for something; your job is to PROVE
things on Token Factory, not assume them, and hand back a report a partner could act on.

Tools, and when to use them:
- list_models: see what Token Factory serves (filter by family if the partner named one). Only use
  model ids that appear in its output; if a requested model is missing, say so and use the nearest.
- run_probe: run a real framework probe in a sandbox against Token Factory. This is the only way to
  claim an integration works. Use it whenever the ask mentions a framework, an integration, or
  "does X work". Prefer pydantic_ai unless the partner names another.
- run_conformance: the 13-check endpoint/model kit (tools, parallel calls, forced choice, json_schema,
  streaming deltas, prefix cache). ALWAYS run it once on the model you recommend: the partner's
  README needs the check table, and it tells you whether the model or the framework is at fault.
- benchmark_model: TTFT and tokens/s on the partner's own prompt. Use for model choice, voice,
  coding agents, or any latency question. Benchmark two candidates when choosing.
- web_search: live facts from the web via Tavily, only when the ask needs them.

Rules:
- A complete run calls run_probe, run_conformance and benchmark (two candidates when choosing a
  model). Skip one only if the partner's ask makes it meaningless, and say so in findings.
- Be concrete. Every finding carries a number or a named check.
- integration_verified is true only if a probe reported tool_called=true.
- If the sandbox is disabled, say so in findings and keep going with what you can measure.
- Say plainly when premium real-time inference is NOT the answer (batch, offline evals, embeddings).
- spoken_summary: at most 60 words, first person, no markdown, as if telling the partner on a call.

The configured default model is Qwen/Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct-2507; when a request says 'the configured model' pass that id."}]

# Coding Agent Framework & Model Recommendation

Generated by Nebius Integration Scout · 2026-11-02 · endpoint https://api.tokenfactory.nebius.com/v1/

**Verdict:** integration verified · recommended model `moonshotai/Kimi-K2.7-Code` · workload coding-agent · no latency budget given

## What was proven
- langgraph on daytona: tool call verified — LangGraph ReAct agent successfully called weather tool with city=Amsterdam
- pydantic_ai on daytona: tool call verified — PydanticAI with typed tool and typed output successfully completed

Conformance kit: 12 pass · 1 partial · 0 fail (cache.cached_tokens=PARTIAL: prefix cache not observable)

## Measured on your prompt
| model | TTFT ms | tokens/s | prefix-cache hit (tokens) |
|---|---|---|---|
| moonshotai/Kimi-K2.7-Code | 1463.8 | 1658.7 | 0 |
| MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash | 3215.2 | 100.3 | 256 |

## Findings
- moonshotai/Kimi-K2.7-Code delivers 1,659 tokens/s, 16.5x faster than MiniMax-M3.1-Flash (100 tokens/s)
- LangGraph and PydanticAI both verified with tool_called=true on Daytona
- Conformance passed 12/13 checks; prefix cache not observable
- Kimi-K2.7-Code TTFT is 1.5s, MiniMax-M3.1-Flash TTFT is 3.2s
- Kimi-K2.7-Code handled parallel tool calls and JSON schema output correctly
- PydanticAI probe used typed tools and structured output with full roundtrip

## Next steps
- Start with PydanticAI for type safety and performance
- Monitor Daytona sandbox stability for long-running agents
- File a ticket to enable prefix caching for Kimi-K2.7-Code
- Run longitudinal benchmarks on full coding tasks

## Cost
add prices to pricing.json for an estimate

## Integration
```python
from langchain_core.tools import tool
from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI
from langgraph.prebuilt import create_react_agent

llm = ChatOpenAI(model="moonshotai/Kimi-K2.7-Code", base_url="https://api.tokenfactory.nebius.com/v1/", api_key=NEBIUS_API_KEY, temperature=0)

@tool
def your_tool(arg: str) -> dict:
    """What the tool does."""
    ...

agent = create_react_agent(llm, [your_tool])
state = agent.invoke({"messages": [("user", "...")]})
```

> We run a coding agent that executes in Daytona sandboxes and makes dozens of sequential model calls per task, so tokens per second is what we feel. Run the langgraph probe and the pydantic_ai probe in the sandbox against moonshotai/Kimi-K2.7-Code (fall back to the configured model if it is not served), run the conformance kit on it, benchmark it and MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash on a code-edit prompt, and tell us which framework to start with and what throughput to expect.
